fig4.claim: Cases in which a continuous carbonate layer was observed have predicted heterogeneous barriers below the critical barrier, and cases without a layer lie above it.
fig4.caption_key: Filled circles: layer observed; open squares: no layer observed. Horizontal bars: range of the predicted barrier over the parameter uncertainty. Vertical line: critical barrier. Case identifiers on the vertical axis are defined in the caption.

fig5.claim: The heterogeneous barrier falls below the critical barrier only at small wetting angle and high supersaturation; the threshold contours bound the region where a layer can nucleate.
fig5.caption_key: Colour: heterogeneous barrier on a logarithmic scale (colour bar). Black contours: the critical-barrier thresholds, whose values the caption gives; the barrier falls towards small wetting angle and high supersaturation.

fig6.claim: A few inputs carry most of the variance of the predicted barrier, and those inputs need the tightest precision from first-principles validation.
fig6.caption_key: (a) Filled circles: first-order index; open diamonds: total-order index; bars: confidence intervals. Inputs are ranked by total-order index. (b) Precision each input must reach, on a logarithmic scale, in the same order.

fig7.claim: The window of pH and potential in which the protective solid phase is stable differs between the two regimes.
fig7.caption_key: (a) First regime, (b) second regime, with their conditions. Fill colour identifies the predominant species; the same species has the same colour in both panels and the caption names each colour. Dashed lines: stability limits of water.
